items.title: The same UPDATE intermittently needs far more shared buffers for about a minute
items.body:
PostgreSQL 17.10 on Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server. A large, high-write OLTP table with more than a dozen indexes, all plain btree, no GIN or other index types. Rows are inserted once, then updated repeatedly as they move through a state machine.

The dominant statement on this table:

UPDATE t
   SET c1=$1, c2=$2,
       status_col=$3,      -- indexed
       counter_col=$4,     -- indexed
       payload_col=$5      -- text, TOASTable
 WHERE t.id=$6;

WHERE is an equality match on the primary key. Because two of the SET columns are indexed, this can never be a HOT update, every execution has to touch every index on the table, not just the heap.

Every so often, for roughly a minute, execution time for these UPDATEs rises significantly and then recovers on its own, with no matching spike in throughput. Query Store shows the direct cause: overall buffers touched per call (shared_blks_hit + shared_blks_read) increases, and most of that increase is in reads.

In the same window, primary-key lookups on this table is not affected, and the query plan itself doesn't change. No triggers fire for this statement. So the problem looks specific to this UPDATE's execution path, not to storage, WAL, or a load spike. Wait events during the episode are dominated by LWLock:BufferContent and IO:DataFileRead.

The only correlation I've found so far, not confident in it, could be coincidence, is that these episodes tend to start shortly after an autovacuum on the table finishes.

What can make the same UPDATE, with the same plan, temporarily need substantially more shared buffers, in a way that self-resolves after about a minute? My working guess is free-space-map churn right after vacuum releases space, but I'd like to know what else in the UPDATE path could cause this.

items.title: Spark task fails with NotLeaderOrReplicaException when writing to Kafka (KRaft) – can broker timeout tuning fix this?
items.body:
We are encountering intermittent failures in our Spark job when writing to Kafka:

Spark task failed due to a NotLeaderOrReplicaException

From what we understand, this occurs when a Kafka broker receives a request for a partition but is no longer the leader (likely due to leader election or metadata lag).

Environment

  • Kafka in KRaft mode (no ZooKeeper)

  • Spark (writing to Kafka)

  • Brokers running on slow disks (RAID/HDD)

  • Moderate-to-high throughput workload

Suspected Root Cause

We suspect the issue is related to:

  • replication lag (slow disk I/O)

  • ISR (in-sync replica) instability

  • frequent leader changes

  • clients (Spark) using slightly stale metadata

We are considering adjusting the following Kafka configurations to improve stability and reduce leader churn:

broker.properties
replica.lag.time.max.ms=60000          # was 10000
replica.socket.timeout.ms=90000        # was commented (default 30000)
replica.fetch.wait.max.ms=500          # was commented — activate explicitly
controlled.shutdown.enable=true        # was commented — activate explicitly
controlled.shutdown.max.retries=5      # was commented (default 3)
controlled.shutdown.retry.backoff.ms=5000
unclean.leader.election.enable=false   # was commented — activate explicitly
leader.imbalance.check.interval.seconds=60  # was commented (default 300)
min.insync.replicas=2       
 
controller.properties
controller.socket.timeout.ms=90000
controlled.shutdown.max.retries=5

Questions

  1. Will increasing replica.lag.time.max.ms and related timeouts (as above) help reduce NotLeaderOrReplicaException in practice?

  2. Are these settings appropriate for environments with slow disks to reduce ISR churn and leader elections?

  3. Are there any risks (e.g., masking real replication issues or delaying failure detection) with using such high timeout values?

  4. In KRaft mode, is there anything else at the controller or broker level that should be tuned to improve leader stability?

  5. Are there additional client-side (Spark/Kafka producer) settings that are critical for handling this condition reliably?

Goal

Our goal is to:

  • reduce leader instability

  • avoid Spark task failures

  • make the system resilient to transient leader changes

items.title: How do I sync SelkoDialog user signals into Mixpanel for segmentation and filtering?
items.body:
I use Mixpanel for analytics and this works great, I can see what users are doing and what is happening in the product.

To understand the real reasons why users do various things, especially why they churn, I use SelkoDialog AI User Interview Agent. This gives me deeper insights about my users and creates AI Signals for each user.

Now I would like to sync these signals into Mixpanel so that I can use them there, for example to:

  • segment users based on the AI Signals

  • use the signals as filters in reports/funnels

  • study specific user groups based on these signals

What is the recommended way to sync external user-level data like this into Mixpanel? Is there some 3rd party Mixpanel-SelkoDialog integration?

If I do this manually myself, should the AI Signals be sent as:

  • user profile properties

  • event properties

  • cohorts

  • or something else?

What is the best practice for keeping these signals updated over time?

items.title: How to implement access control for Feature Views in Snowflake Feature Store without separate stores per team?
items.body:
Problem

In a shared Snowflake Feature Store, fs.list_feature_views() returns all Feature Views regardless of which team owns them. There is no native way to scope access to a subset of Feature Views within a single schema — calling list_feature_views() always exposes every FV to every team.

Concrete scenario:

Team A owns sensitive fraud detection features (transaction_features_fv, user_risk_scores_fv). Team B works on churn prediction features. Both teams share the same Feature Store / schema

fs = FeatureStore(
  session=session, 
  database="ML_DB", 
  name="SHARED_FS", 
  default_warehouse="ML_WH"
)

This returns ALL Feature Views from both teams — no way to filter by ownership all_fvs = fs.list_feature_views()

Team A's sensitive Feature Views are visible to Team B and vice versa.

What I've tried

1. Separate Feature Store per team — enforces isolation, but breaks cross-team feature sharing (Team B cannot reuse Team A's non-sensitive features).

2. Individual object-level grants — Snowflake RBAC grants on individual Feature View objects don't integrate with the FeatureStore Python SDK; list_feature_views() still returns all FVs regardless of role grants.

3. Naming conventions + scripted grants — e.g. prefixing Feature View names with the owning team (FRAUD__transaction_features$V1_0) and writing custom grant scripts per naming group. This works at the SQL layer but is brittle, not enforced by the SDK, and requires manual maintenance as teams and FVs grow.

What I'm looking for

Is there a supported or idiomatic way in the Snowflake ML SDK (or via SQL/RBAC) to:

  1. Group Feature Views by team/domain within a single Feature Store schema, and

  2. Restrict list_feature_views() / access to only the Feature Views a given role should see?

  3. Something analogous to:

python
# Hypothetical — does anything like this exist today?
fs.list_feature_views(group="FRAUD_DETECTION")

Or is the only production-ready solution currently to use separate Feature Stores per team, accepting the cross-team sharing limitation?
